National dropped income tax more than they raised GST so those employees are still making more money, and in general GST has been used to lower the burden of income tax in the 80's too.

No they didn't. Before 2009 the income tax rate was 12.5% on 0-$14,000, and 21% on $14,000-48,000.

National changed that to 10.5% and 17.5%. That means for someone earning 30k their tax bill goes from $5110 to $4270 or an $840 cut. 

Even if they spent every cent of their money on GST taxable items (which is completely unrealistic, it's just to prove a point) a 2.5% raise in GST amounts to $643.25 on an after tax income of $25,730.

The reason that's completely unrealistic though, is that housing is GST exempt and low income earners pay a higher % of their income towards it. That means they effectively don't pay GST on most of what they spend.

My unpopular opinion on the matter is that farming always will be dangerous and attempts to change that lead to worse staff as opposed to less danger. 

I worked on a hill country sheep and beef farm where noone wore helmets on anything and everyone who worked there knew how to bail off a rolling quad cause it happened to all of us at least once, and noone ever got seriously hurt. That was partly down to luck but you also build a lot more skill putting yourself in danger constantly.

If you start to over analyze what you do on a farm everything becomes a hazard because there's unavoidable dangers everywhere.

Some off the top of my head are water tank and gutter cleaning(can be done yourself but really important if you're on rain water), pumping sewerage, depending on how much land you get fencing, and if you get animals that opens another can of worms.

There's probably a bit around building but that'll be situation specific.
